Interactive figures from my work. Everything here runs in your browser; the
underlying series are prepared in R and live as CSV in `data/` in the
[site's repository](https://github.com/REEMPLAZAR).

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
The figure below uses **synthetic placeholder data**, not estimates. It is here
to show the format while real series are prepared.
:::

## Informality rate by state

::: {.eyebrow}
Placeholder · Source to be added
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
raw = FileAttachment("data/informality-example.csv").csv({ typed: true })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof picked = Inputs.checkbox(
  [...new Set(raw.map(d => d.state))].sort(),
  {
    label: "States",
    value: ["Oaxaca", "Nuevo León", "Jalisco", "Ciudad de México"]
  }
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
filtered = raw.filter(d => picked.includes(d.state))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  width: 820,
  height: 420,
  marginLeft: 52,
  marginBottom: 40,
  // currentColor y fondo transparente: la grafica sigue el tema claro/oscuro
  // del sitio sin duplicar paleta.
  style: { fontFamily: "IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif", fontSize: "13px",
           color: "currentColor", background: "transparent" },
  x: { label: "", tickFormat: "d" },
  y: { label: "Informality rate (%)", grid: true, nice: true },
  color: { legend: true, scheme: "Tableau10" },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.3 }),
    Plot.lineY(filtered, {
      x: "year", y: "informality_rate", stroke: "state",
      strokeWidth: 2, curve: "monotone-x"
    }),
    Plot.dot(filtered, {
      x: "year", y: "informality_rate", fill: "state", r: 3
    }),
    Plot.tip(filtered, Plot.pointer({
      x: "year", y: "informality_rate",
      title: d => `${d.state}\n${d.year}: ${d.informality_rate}%`
    }))
  ]
})
```

<details class="abstract">
<summary>How this is built</summary>

**1. Prepare a tidy CSV in R.** One row per observation, short lowercase column
names. The script lives in `scripts/` and is run by hand, so the site itself
stays free of any computational engine and renders on any machine:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)   # ENOE is a complex survey: use the design, not a raw mean

tabla <- enoe |>
  as_survey_design(ids = upm, strata = est_d_tri, weights = fac_tri, nest = TRUE) |>
  group_by(ent, year) |>
  summarise(informality_rate = survey_mean(informal == 1, na.rm = TRUE) * 100)

write_csv(tabla, here::here("data", "informality-example.csv"))
```

Run it with `Rscript scripts/01-informality-by-state.R`.

**2. Point the chart at the file.** Change the filename in the first `{ojs}`
block and the column names in the `Plot.lineY` call.

**3. Preview.** Run `quarto preview`; the chart updates as you save. Observable
and Observable Plot ship inside Quarto and run in the reader's browser, so no
runtime is needed to publish.

For figures that belong in a paper, write them with `ggplot2` in the same script
and `ggsave()` an SVG into `images/`, then use standard markdown. Interactive
versions earn their place only when the reader gains something from choosing a
state, a cohort, or a year.

</details>
